data.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says — Update
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases given the current economic outlook after the central bank voted to hold interest rates steady this week, according to Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.

Without any monetary-policy restraint, inflation will continue to trend above target unless unexpected shocks occur, Logan said at an event in Davidson, N.C., on Friday.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate," she added.

There had been speculation that Logan would dissent at October's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, given her previous calls for tighter monetary policy and a previous dissent she gave in July. On Friday, she offered more explanation to why she instead supported the committee's decision to hold interest rates where they are.

Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology-investment outlook and geopolitical developments, she said. In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary, she added.

Moreover, Logan said the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay as long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans.

In addition, skipping a meeting of rate increases doesn't change the monetary-policy destination, Logan argued.

"By making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip," she explained.

Given the current outlook, the end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive to sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices, Logan said.

Write to Jessica Coacci at jessica.coacci@wsj.com

data.title: W.Africa Crude-Grades end week steady
data.description:
West African crude oil differentials were little changed on Friday, though an uptick in Chinese buying could be providing a floor to differentials, traders said.

  • Chinese demand was helping to slow the slide in West African differentials, two traders said, after mounting pressure in recent weeks from record-high freight rates. West African grades tend to travel long-haul to their main demand outlets

  • However, the overhang of November cargoes will have to clear before pressure in the West African crude market can really let up, one of the traders added

  • November cargoes are waiting to clear while December loading schedules are already out

  • Exports of four key Nigerian crude oil grades are expected to increase. They are estimated to average 888,000 bpd in December versus 874,000 bpd in November, preliminary programmes showed

  • There were no bids or offers for West African crudes in the Platts window on Friday, another trader said

  • In downstream news, Cameroon's state oil refiner Sonara said on Friday that it had signed an agreement with Nigeria's Dangote Group and Lagos-based MRS Oil & Gas Company to supply refined petroleum products to Cameroon

data.title: ExxonMobil to Invest in its Refineries to Boost Margins: CEO — OPIS
data.description:
ExxonMobil will focus on investing in projects at its existing facilities including the Baton Rouge, La., and Beaumont, Texas, refineries to improve the production yields and increase refined product margins, Chief Executive Darren Woods said Friday.

In the company's third-quarter earnings call with analysts, Woods said that the oil major has been investing "selectively" in its large refineries which have portfolios of high-value production like lubricants, chemicals and petroleum products.

While ExxonMobil has homed in on upgrading its product slate and improving the yield for its traditional petroleum products, the company is looking more broadly at other hydrocarbons like Proxxima — its polyolefin thermoset resin used in composite and coatings — and carbon materials.

"We will continue to look for ways that we can leverage existing facilities to continue to make products that have high margins, high value in the short term," Woods said.

Investing in existing refineries allows ExxonMobil to increase production capacity at roughly half the cost compared with building a brand-new facility, he said.

"So today, we're investing in Baytown. Our plans include investments in Baton Rouge and Beaumont, and that will significantly improve our production of diesel, chemical feedstocks, and lubricants," Woods said.

The oil major has increased its crude processing capacity by nearly 10% since 2019, and its 637,400 b/d Beaumont, Texas, refinery boosted its distillate production by about 40% following the completion of a $2 billion expansion project in early 2023. In addition, the company has a current project to increase distillate and lubricant production in its 588,000 b/d Baytown, Texas, refinery.

Looking forward, ExxonMobil expects its investments across its U.S. facilities will increase distillate production by another 100,000 b/d, said Woods, without providing a specific time period.

In its upstream segment, the major expects full-year production in the Permian Basin in West Texas of around 1.8 million oil-equivalent b/d. In late Q4, the company will start up its fifth floating production, storage, and offloading vessel in Guyana that is key to increasing output.

ExxonMobil also expects Q4 Middle East production impacts in line with Q3, or around 350,000 of oil-equivalent b/d being offline, assuming continuation of the current level of supply disruptions.

data.title: TGTX Stock Hits Fresh 52-Week High Ahead Of Earnings Amid Buyout Buzz
data.description:
Key points:
  • According to data from Fiscal AI, analysts forecast roughly $0.36 in earnings per share and about $245 million in revenue.
  • In late August, rumors emerged that a U.S. biopharma with a market cap between $20 billion and $40 billion may be interested in acquiring TG Therapeutics; the company didn't confirm the rumors. 
  • Besides commercializing intravenous Briumvi, TG is also testing a subcutaneous version of the drug and a CAR-T therapy azer-cel.

Shares of TG Therapeutics (TGTX) jumped on Friday, setting a new 52-week high, advancing a multi-day climb ahead of the company’s third-quarter earnings and amid buyout rumors.

The stock was trading 5% higher at the time of writing.

TGTX’s Upcoming Earnings

Investors are now focused on the company’s projected third-quarter 2026 results, estimated for Monday, November 2. The company has not confirmed the date.

According to data from Fiscal AI, analysts forecast roughly $0.36 in earnings per share and about $245 million in revenue. In the prior quarter, the company beat revenue expectations but missed on EPS while raising full-year guidance on BRIUMVI sales.

BRIUMVI is the company’s sole approved product indicated for adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, a chronic, autoimmune disease of the central nervous system causing nerve damage. It is given as a one-hour intravenous infusion every 24 weeks after the initial doses and has gained regulatory clearance in the United States and several other markets. Recent quarterly results showed continued double-digit sequential growth in U.S. net sales, supporting raised annual revenue targets near $950 million globally.

TG Therapeutics’ Pipeline Updates

Besides commercializing intravenous Briumvi, TG is also testing a subcutaneous version of the drug and a CAR-T therapy, azer-cel.

On October 23, the company presented early-stage data for azer-cel in progressive multiple sclerosis at the MSToronto2026 meeting. In 26 treated participants, the regimen showed no high-grade CAR-T toxicities. Among evaluable patients, 89% had stable or improved disability scores at day 90, with evidence of B-cell depletion in blood and cerebrospinal fluid.

According to data from Koyfin, seven of eight analysts covering TGTX rate it 'Buy' or higher, while one rates it 'Strong Sell.' The stock has a 12-month average price target of $69.71, representing a potential upside of over 10% from the stock’s last close.

In late August, rumors emerged that a U.S. biopharma with a market cap between $20 billion and $40 billion may be interested in acquiring TG Therapeutics. The company didn't confirm the rumors.

How Did Stocktwits Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TGTX stock jumped from 'bullish' to 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'high' levels.

A Stocktwits user voiced anticipation for a buyout for $15-$20 billion, noting that he is “not convinced, but it is possible.” He also highlighted the strong addressable market for Briumvi, once the subcutaneous version of the drug is also approved. Currently, only the intravenous version is commercially available; the subcutaneous version is in late-stage development.

View this Stocktwits post

Another user, however, pinned the rally to good earnings instead of buyout anticipation.

View this Stocktwits post

TGTX has more than doubled year-to-date.

data.title: Fed Officials Signal December Rate Increase Remains on Track — WSJ
data.description:
By Nick Timiraos

Three Federal Reserve officials on Friday signaled support for continuing to raise interest rates, most likely at the central bank's next meeting in December, after having held them steady this week.

"Skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination," said Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, in remarks delivered to college students Friday that were released by the bank.

Logan voted in favor of the decision to hold steady this week. The last time the Fed held rates steady, in July, Logan dissented in favor of a rate increase. The Fed raised rates in September. Two of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented this week in favor of a rate increase.

Logan repeated her view that the Fed needs to make at least two more increases of a quarter point. She said moving gradually made sense after recent market swings and because the timing of any increase matters less if investors understand where the Fed is ultimately headed.

After making two additional rate increases, she said, "it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate."

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who isn't a voter on policy this year, said he judged "additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon." Without further increases, he said inflation would likely stay well above the Fed's 2% target over the next 18 months.

During remarks in New York, Musalem spelled out what it would take to convince him to hold off. Inflation could ease without more Fed rate increases if energy prices and shipping costs fall. Demand could also slow more than expected if spending on the AI build-out drops sharply or if a sudden pullback in financial markets leads wealthier households to retrench. Musalem said he saw this scenario as "less likely but plausible."

Both officials signaled little concern about recent turbulence in financial markets. Logan said the run-up in long-term interest rates this year mostly reflects investors' expectations of stronger growth, a sign that "monetary policy has work to do."

Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin told Sirius XM Business Radio a "gradual approach" to raising rates made sense because the Fed is "not much behind the curve."

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
